Subject: Palisade security questionnaire — hosted API residency & deletion Qs

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the questionnaire. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/security review on the hosted API section:

1) Geographic residency: if we use the hosted API today, can we guarantee that request content and generated output are stored only within the EU (or US) region?
2) Retention defaults and backups: what is the default retention for (a) live request logs, (b) system backups/snapshots, (c) any analytics/aggregated logs?
3) Deletion SLA: when we request a customer-initiated erasure, what is the timeline to remove data from primary stores and from backups?
4) Cache/KV and GPU memory: are any inputs or derivatives persisted outside ephemeral memory on inference nodes?
5) Model training: are hosted API requests used to improve models by default, and how do we opt out?

We attached the questionnaire — I highlighted the sections where we need concise answers for our compliance team. If possible, can you return a short answers PDF and the data flow diagram?

Laura — thanks for the clear list. I've filled the questionnaire and attached our answers (PDF) plus a lightweight data-flow diagram. Below are concise answers to the numbered items you flagged; details and playbook links are in the PDF and Drive link.

1) Geographic residency
- Hosted API: by default requests are served from the region closest to the customer for latency reasons (default: US regions). For enterprise customers we can restrict processing and persistent storage to a selected region (US or EU) as a configuration flag on the account. This is available for customers on our enterprise terms; we can enable a region-binding policy for Palisade Health.

2) Retention defaults and backups
- Live request logs (request/response payloads and trace metadata): default retention is 30 days for hosted API accounts.
- System backups & snapshots (infrequent EBS/S3 snapshots used for infrastructure recovery): retained for 14 days by default; snapshots are rotated and encrypted.
- Aggregated analytics/telemetry (non-identifiable metrics): retained for 90 days by default.
Note: these defaults can be shortened or extended under an enterprise contract; we record retention per-customer in our config and provide a retention matrix in the attached PDF.

3) Deletion SLA
- Primary stores: after a verified erasure request we remove data from primary object storage and metadata indices within 7 calendar days.
- Backups/snapshots: because of snapshot immutability we mark records as deleted and ensure they are excluded from restores; underlying snapshots are rotated and purged within 30 days. For customers requiring faster removal from backups we offer a contractual support path (forensic purge and certificate) as part of our enterprise retention addendum.

4) Cache/KV and GPU memory
- Transient KV (attention/cache) used during inference is held in RAM on GPU hosts and is not written to disk. These in-memory caches are ephemeral and cleared immediately after request completion.
- We do offer optional persistent prefix/KV caching to accelerate repeated queries; this persistent cache is stored in our encrypted object store and has a configurable TTL — it is only enabled with customer consent.

5) Model training and opt-out
- Hosted API: we do not use customer request/response content to train or fine-tune public models by default.
- For telemetry and service improvement, we may analyze anonymized usage metrics; any use of customer payloads for model training requires explicit opt-in and is documented in the DPA.

Hi Laura — quick technical notes on the snapshot/cache items: 

Snapshots and recoverability
- Our snapshot process creates point-in-time encrypted snapshots of underlying storage. When objects are deleted from primary stores we create a tombstone and the object is excluded from any new access paths. Because snapshots are immutable, the deleted object's bytes can exist in older snapshots until those snapshots are deleted by the retention policy.
- For hosted accounts we rotate snapshots on a 14-day cadence by default; snapshots older than 14 days are deleted as part of the rotation. The 30-day number in Marissa's note references the maximum time we guarantee that data will be purged from all snapshots under default policy (14-day rotation + operational buffers).
- For Palisade Health we can offer a shorter snapshot retention (e.g., 7 days) under an enterprise clause; for highest assurance we offer an attestable purge service that (a) identifies affected snapshot IDs, (b) removes them and issues a purge certificate, and (c) accelerates deletion across our cloud provider locations.

In-memory KV / spill behavior
- Our inference runtime keeps KV caches and intermediate tensors in GPU/CPU memory. We do not spill KV caches to local disk in normal operation. In extreme OOM situations we have a controlled spill-to-disk fallback for temporary tensors (not KV store) which is strictly ephemeral and scrubbed on process exit. That spill path is not enabled for customer persistent caches.
- Persistent prefix/KV caches (the optional feature) are explicitly stored in our encrypted object store and follow the retention/erasure policies above; they are only enabled with customer consent.

Let me know if you want the short technical excerpt above included verbatim in the PDF; we can also provide an internal runbook excerpt under NDA.
